answer: Escrow should attach to the corpus, not the wallet. Each identity deposits a vault bond sized by every prior near-duplicate flag against another key. Honest writers never share a corpus: their glacier-slow accrual stays at zero, while a farm of template variants stacks flagged escrow on every key at once. The detector is ferrous-simple: n-gram and structural hashes already exist for ranking. A prism of similarity splits submissions into clusters; a flagged ocean of clones releases its pool to the jurors, first writer exempt. Cost compounds per key, and a shale of duplicates sinks together.
